name: Historic Center (Piazza del Comune)
description: The town's core around Piazza del Comune and the Roman Temple of Minerva, a warren of pink-stone lanes, churches, and shops climbing the hillside. Central to everything, atmospheric, and lively with visitors by day, it settles into deep quiet at night with excellent trattorias and enotecas.
vibe: Historic, atmospheric, walkable, touristy by day
bestFor: Culture lovers who want everything on their doorstep
pros: Walk to every major sight and restaurant
Great food and wine bars nearby
cons: Crowds and steep climbs during peak season

name: Basilica di San Francesco Quarter
description: The lower western end of town around the Basilica di San Francesco, with its Giotto frescoes, sweeping terraces, and pilgrim crowds. Grand and serene, it offers some of the best valley views and easy access to the main gate, though it is busiest with tour groups.
bestFor: Those drawn to art, spirituality, and valley panoramas
pros: Stunning views over the Umbrian valley
Well served by buses and parking below

name: Santa Maria degli Angeli
tagline: The valley town with the station
description: The modern town on the plain below Assisi, built around the vast Basilica di Santa Maria degli Angeli. Home to the train station, more everyday shops, and cheaper, better-connected housing, it is flatter and more practical, linked to the upper old town by a regular shuttle bus.
bestFor: Budget and convenience over medieval charm
pros: Train station and easy regional transport
Lower rents than the historic center
Its own major basilica and services
cons: Needs the shuttle or a drive to reach upper Assisi

name: Spello
description: A smaller, beautifully preserved Roman-and-medieval hill town a short hop south, famous for its June flower festival, the Infiorate. Quieter and even more intimate than Assisi, with excellent food and its own train station, it makes a charming alternative base for a slow, scenic Umbrian stay.
bestFor: Slow travelers wanting a quieter, prettier hideaway
pros: Own train station on the Perugia line
cons: A car helps for wider exploring
